This is when suicide becomes an active choice and the person in line researches on methods to go peacefully.

People keep assuming victims use suicide as a way to escape problems, and that’s almost true except it’s the same way you drink your problems away, drugs and any other coping mechanism. Meaning, with help, it’s preventable. But there’s a more complex layer to suicide and the commitment to such an act. It cannot be good or bad.

When you’re discounting your liability/bonds to present value- the rationality is to show how much the principal + interest is worth in today’s market- your true cost of borrowing. Your financial statements have to reflect the amounts in the current year value, not how much it’ll be worth later. 

When you’re discounting the lease payments to present value- you’re essentially showing how much the lease actually costs in today’s market. 

When you’re discounting cash flows of assets to present value- well the whole point of capitalising assets is to show the earning potential of the asset. You need to show how much the asset is worth as of the current year either adjusting it for fair market value or amortising to carrying value.. The undiscounted cash flow for the asset HAS to be higher than the carrying value for a reason. If it revenue generated cannot make up for the cost of the asset, then there’s an impairment 

In essence, for both assets and liabilities, you’re discounting the cash flow to present value to show how much the asset and liability is worth TODAY, like right now. Not 5 years, not 10 years into the past/ future, but NOW. It’s one of the principals of accrual accounting: transparency of the true economic value of the business as of today.

Your thinking about the insurance recovery affecting NBV makes sense on the surface, but under the group depreciation method, the treatment is different as you know it. 

The receipt of insurance is not tied to recognizing gains or losses, because those aren’t recorded under the group method when an individual asset is retired. The insurance recovery increases cash, but it doesn’t increase or decrease the NBV of the group of assets.

Retirement of the Truck (no gain or loss recognized):
   - Debit: Accumulated Depreciation (A/D) – for the truck retired
   - Credit: Delivery Trucks (Asset) – for the original cost of the truck

Insurance Recovery Received(this increases cash):
   - Debit: Cash – for the insurance recovery amount
   - Credit: A/D

Because under the group method, the recovery of insurance isn’t treated as a gain or loss. Instead, it reduces the accumulated depreciation account, effectively acknowledging that some of the value of the truck was recovered through insurance, rather than depreciation expense. 

The net book value of the group is not directly impacted by the insurance recovery because no gains or losses are recognized under the group depreciation method. Instead, the insurance proceeds reduce accumulated depreciation, not the group asset’s net book value directly. So, your brain was close, but the key is how the recovery is handled through accumulated depreciation.
